title: Materialized Views & Concurrent Refresh
description: Cache expensive analytical queries on disk with Materialized Views, and refresh without locking reads using CONCURRENTLY.

data.text: Unlike a standard view, a **Materialized View** physically executes the query and stores the resulting rows on disk. Subsequent queries against the materialized view execute in sub-milliseconds without recalculating complex joins or aggregations.
The Power of `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`

A standard refresh locks the materialized view from all reads while rebuilding. However, if you create a unique index on the materialized view, you can refresh it **CONCURRENTLY**, allowing applications to continue querying the cached view with zero downtime!

data.title: Materialized View with Concurrent Refresh Setup
data.content: Daily sales metrics with unique index for non-blocking refreshes.
data.code:
-- 1. Create Materialized View
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW daily_sales_summary AS
SELECT 
    DATE(created_at) AS sale_date,
    product_category,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    SUM(total_amount) AS revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY DATE(created_at), product_category;

-- 2. Create UNIQUE index (Mandatory for CONCURRENT refresh)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_daily_sales_unique ON daily_sales_summary (sale_date, product_category);

-- 3. Non-blocking refresh triggered via cron or scheduler
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY daily_sales_summary;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Materialized views persist query results physically to disk.
Create indexes directly on materialized views for high-performance seeks.
Always create a `UNIQUE` index to enable non-blocking `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY`.
